html:
In 1961 Wallis and Futuna became an overseas territory of France, after its people voted for it in 1959. Before that the islands had been a French protectorate since the late 1880s.

The law kept the three traditional kingdoms: ʻUvea on Wallis, and Alo and Sigave on Futuna. Their kings and chiefs still settle land and custom, beside the French administrator and an elected assembly. The Catholic Church runs much of the schooling.

Jobs are few, and more Wallisians and Futunians now live in New Caledonia than on the islands themselves, many having gone to work in its nickel mines.
